IDAGIO is the leading streaming service for classical music, based in Berlin and part of IDAGIO Group. The Group spans streaming, recordings, and live music partnerships, globally. Our director initiates projects across all of it: recording partnerships with orchestras, licensing talks with international labels, concert-hall collaborations in Taiwan and Japan, and new ventures.
These initiatives move fast and span many time zones. We are looking for the person at the director's side who keeps them all on track.
Tasks
You are the assistant to the sole director of IDAGIO Group and work with him daily. He travels extensively and meets industry leaders, orchestras, and institutions across Asia, Europe and the US. Every trip produces introductions, ideas, and commitments. Your job is to make sure none of them get lost. You track every thread, follow up with every party, and hold everyone to agreed deadlines, including the director.
Beyond that, you coordinate selected projects across the Group's Berlin companies, working with their Managing Directors. Decisions sit with the director and the Managing Directors. Keeping things moving sits with you.
Assistant and project support to the director
Track and follow up on the projects and partnerships the director runs across the Group. You keep an up-to-date overview of status, owners, and next steps at all times.
Maintain deadlines and flag slipping dates early. You chase open items without being asked.
Prepare agendas, briefings, and follow-ups for meetings. Maintain trackers and status summaries.
Coordinate scheduling, information flow, and documentation across internal and external stakeholders, from orchestra managements to distribution partners.
Project coordination for Moto Lab
Moto Lab Partners is the Group's newest venture: it supports classical artists and institutions in building their international presence and careers, from recordings and concert videos to release strategy and promotion.
Coordinate Moto Lab's projects from start to finish, whatever their shape: a release, a concert video production, a marketing campaign, or a partner engagement.
Act as the central point of contact between everyone involved: artists and their management, orchestras, production crews, distributors, agencies, and internal teams.
Track each project's timeline from planning through delivery, follow up on deliverables, and support project and budget administration until everything is complete and approved.

Several years of professional experience, typically 2 to 5, in an assistant, coordination, project management, or artist management role. This should not be your first job. You have managed deadlines across multiple stakeholders and worked alongside a demanding senior principal before.
A firm understanding of classical music and the industry around it: repertoire, orchestras, how recordings and releases work. A background in classical music (studies, an orchestra, a label, an agency, a concert hall) is a strong plus.
Proactive and organized by temperament. You take ownership, chase without being prompted, and flag problems early.
Comfortable running several projects in parallel and prioritizing against deadlines.
Clear, structured communication and documentation. Status is transparent to everyone at any time.
Fluent German and English (C1 or better, spoken and written). Japanese or Mandarin is a real plus given our partners in Japan and Taiwan.
Based in Berlin or willing to relocate. Occasional flexibility for calls with Asia or the US and for concert or recording dates in the evening.

A rare vantage point: you work directly with the director of a music group active between Europe and Asia, and you see every initiative across it.
Real responsibility from day one. The role exists because these projects matter and need an owner.
A small, senior, international team in Berlin with short decision paths.
Salary range: €42,000–50,000 gross/year, depending on experience.
Send a short cover note, your CV, and your earliest possible start date to apply. Tell us about one person or project you supported where your follow-through made the difference.
IDAGIO and the IDAGIO Group value diversity. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements.

About M3: A Japanese global leader in the provision of ground-breaking and innovative technological and research solutions to the healthcare industry.

The M3 Group operates in the US, Asia, and Europe with over 5.8 million physician members globally via its physician websites which include mdlinx.com, m3.com, research.m3.com, Doctors.net.uk, medigate.net, and medlive.cn.

M3 Inc. is a publicly traded company on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (jp:2413, NIKKEI 225) with subsidiaries in major markets including the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, and China, and in 2020 was ranked in Forbes’ Global 2000 list. The M3 Group provides services to healthcare and the life science industry.

In addition to market research, these services include medical education, ethical drug promotion, clinical development, job recruitment, and clinic appointment services. M3 has offices in Japan, UK, France, Germany, Brazil, Sweden, China, USA, and South Korea, as well as India.

This role is part of MED PLANET , a Lyon based fieldwork agency and a wholly owned subsidiary of M3 Inc. MED PLANET is a leading provider of data-collection services for the pharmaceutical and healthcare industry. We specialize in conducting both qualitative and quantitative market research in France. MED PLANET provides high quality translations and transcription for healthcare fieldwork projects for the M3MR group.
Job Description
As a Project Manager in our translations department, you will be responsible for managing several language-related projects simultaneously, ensuring that they are delivered on time, meeting quality expectations and within scope.

With effective written and verbal communication, you will help ensure the teams are clear on the scope and expectations of clients and that the clients are kept fully informed as to the progress and status of their projects.

You will work closely with our project management team, language professionals, to seek guidance when required and ensure project success.
Support in planning, execution, and monitoring several language-related projects simultaneously using project management tools to ensure that projects are delivered on time and within scope.
Support in maintaining and creating project schedules, and timelines ensuring that they are in line with SLAs and achievable and that they reflect the clients' requirements and expectations.
Monitor project progress on progress, challenges and/or successes throughout the project
Support in maintaining project documentation, including project plans, reports, and communications, using document management software such as SharePoint, etc., to ensure that we have accurate records of our projects.
Prepare quotes and invoices using project management software and accounting software to ensure that we generate revenue and meet our business goals.
Ensure adherence to company standards and procedures in project management to maintain our reputation for delivering high-quality language services.
Identify errors and areas of improvement and report when needed to the relevant stakeholders.
Support during meetings, documenting these when required and distributing minutes/actions to the team.

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as business, management, or language studies.
2 or more years of experience in managing localisation projects.
Essential fluency in English. an additional language would be advantageous.
Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks and work under pressure to meet our clients' needs and achieve our business objectives.
Additional Information
Note: this will be an independent contractor position

You will ensure all project milestones, virtual tabletop exercises, after-action reports, and progress deliverables are completed on time, within scope, and in full compliance with federal quality and accessibility standards. Key Responsibilities
Contract Governance & Project Leadership: Oversee daily operations across all contract tasks, managing schedules, team workflows, sub-contractors, and quality control to meet all performance objectives.
Client & Stakeholder Communication: Serve as the primary operational liaison to the COR and agency leadership; facilitate post-award kickoff meetings, monthly touchpoints, and regular progress briefings.

Key Personnel Status: Demonstrated track record of serving in client-facing leadership roles on federal government contracts.
Technical Skills: Strong proficiency in project management software (MS Project, Asana, or similar), MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), and virtual meeting platforms (Teams, Zoom, Webex).
Compliance Knowledge: Practical understanding of federal contract administration, Quality Control Plans (QCP), and Section 508 document accessibility compliance standards.
Communication: Exceptional oral and written communication skills with proven ability to interface effectively with federal leadership, clinical/technical SMEs, and multidisciplinary teams.

Experience working with or supporting federal health agencies (e.g., HHS, IHS, CDC, SAMHSA).

## Introduction ##
Pour notre division **Systèmes d'information**, nous recherchons un **Responsable de projets (H/F)** dont la mission principale sera de piloter la mise en oeuvre de projets depuis l'expression du besoin jusqu'au déploiement et au suivi opérationnel.

* Conduire, optimiser et être garant de l'ensemble des ressources du projet/ programme (humains, budget, clientèle, décision finale)

* Assumer l'alignement du projet/ programme aux besoins des métiers
* Organiser, coordonner et animer l'équipe projet/ programme
* Arbitrer les éventuels différends entre l'équipe et les autres intervenants
* Superviser le déroulement du projet
* Coordonner, synthétiser et assurer la qualité des validations prononcées
* Gérer la relation avec les fournisseurs
## *Profil* ##
* Diplôme d'une école d'Ingénieur (Master HES ou EPF)
* Expérience de 3 à 5 ans en gestion de projets, idéalement dans un environnement industriel exigeant
* Expérience dans la conduite de projets s'appuyant sur des pratiques et/ ou méthodes Agiles
* De langue maternelle française avec des bonnes connaissances d'anglais
* Bonne maîtrise des outils et systèmes informatiques
* Maîtrise avérée des approches prédictives et Agiles, ainsi que des outils de gestion de projet
* Rigoureux, autonome, organisé et doté d-un fort sens des responsabilités
* Excellentes capacités d-analyse et de synthèse
* Capacité à adapter l-approche de pilotage au contexte, aux enjeux et au niveau de maturité des équipes
* Esprit d-ouverture et goût du travail en équipe
* Très bonnes aptitudes en communication, leadership naturel et sens du service client
* Grande capacité d-adaptation, essentielle pour appréhender un domaine spécifique à notre activité et piloter des projets variés
## Conclusion ##
Nous vous offrons un environnement stimulant, d-excellentes conditions de travail et des prestations sociales de premier ordre.
Nous vous remercions d'adresser un dossier de candidature complet (CV, lettre de motivation, certificats et diplômes).

s.h: Supervisory Responsibilities 25% or more of the time.
s.t:
In order to qualify, you must meet the eligibility and qualifications requirements as defined below by the closing date of the announcement. For more information on the qualifications for this position, visit the Office of Personnel Management's General Schedule Qualification Standards.

Your application and resume must clearly show that you possess the experience requirements. Transcripts must be provided for qualifications based on education. Provide course descriptions as necessary. This is an interdisciplinary position and may be filled in any of the job series listed below.

Basic Requirement: GS-0101 Series: Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in behavioral or social science; or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

OR Combination of education and experience -- that provided the applicant with knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

OR Four years of appropriate experience that demonstrated that the applicant has acquired knowledge of one or more of the behavioral or social sciences equivalent to a major in the field.

GS-0110 Series: Degree: Successfully completed a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus.

OR Combination of education and experience that included 24 semester hours in course work equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education sufficient to demonstrate that I possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform work in the occupation that is comparable to that normally acquired through the successful completion of a full 4-year course of study with a major in the appropriate field needed to perform the work of the occupation.

Examples of appropriate experience to qualify in the Economics series include: Individual economic research assignments requiring planning, information assembly, analysis and evaluation, conclusions and report preparation; Supervisory or project coordination assignments involving a staff of professional economists, and requiring the evaluation and interpretation of economic information; OR Teaching assignments in a college or university that included both class instruction in economics subjects and one of the following: (1) personal research that produced evidence of results, (2) direction of graduate theses in economics, or (3) service as a consultant or advisor on technical economics problems.

Basic Requirements: GS-0401 Series: Degree: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

OR A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a major field of study that included 24 semester hours in course work in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position.

Related course work generally refers to courses that may be accepted as part of the program major.

OR A combination of education and experience that included 24 semester hours in course work in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry or related disciplines appropriate to the position, AND experience sufficient to demonstrate that I possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform work in the occupation that is comparable to that normally acquired through the successful completion of a full 4-year course of study with a major in the appropriate field needed to perform the work of the position.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement, you must also possess experience and/or directly related education in the amounts listed below. Specialized Experience Requirement: For the GS-14 level: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 in the Federal service.

Qualifying specialized experience is defined as three or more of the following: Applies knowledge of natural resources research practices and techniques to convey information concerning scientific topics, policies, and programs to key publics with diverse levels of understanding of scientific disciplines, programs and activities Initiates high priority special projects, studies, and initiatives that affect critical aspects of organizational programs.

Implements natural resource programs and projects including programming, budgeting, and administering the organization's program of work. Provides advice, briefings, assistance and counsel to leadership on responding to the media and/or congressional staff on scientific topics and program activities.

For the GS-15 level: Applicants must have one year specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 in the Federal service.

Qualifying specialized experience is defined as all of the following: Applies knowledge of natural resources research practices and techniques to convey information concerning scientific topics, policies, and programs to key publics with diverse levels of understanding of scientific disciplines, programs and activities.

Develops and directs short and long-range programs and projects including programming, budgeting, and administering the organization's program of work. Reviews scientific research findings and makes recommendations to improve to a natural resources program's content, and methods of investigating research problems.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

TIME IN GRADE REQUIREMENT: If you are a current federal employee in the General Schedule (GS) pay plan and applying for a promotion opportunity, you must meet time-in-grade (TIG) requirements of 52 weeks of service at the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

This requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

* Driven, passionate, ambitious

* Keep one step ahead of changes and have a good sense of the future of the Brands.
* Team player and work well in a matrix organization to share insights and to develop the propositions
* Speaks clearly and fluently; makes presentations and undertakes public speaking with skill and confidence / is able to take complex information and explain things in simple terms to people who are not familiar with the complexity

Global Trials Optimization Specialist
Sponsor Dedicated/ Remote - US only
Are you energized by using data, planning, and cross-functional collaboration to help clinical trials enroll successfully? We’re seeking a Global Trials Optimization Specialist to support program feasibility, recruitment and retention planning, and in-life trial optimization across global clinical studies.
In this role, you’ll help translate trial goals, country input, modeling data, and enrollment insights into practical strategies that support study execution. You’ll partner with clinical trial teams, vendors, legal, analytics, and other stakeholders to identify enrollment opportunities, address challenges, and support patient- and site-facing recruitment efforts.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys combining clinical trial operations, feasibility strategy, recruitment planning, stakeholder coordination, and performance analysis to help studies reach the right participants.

Program Feasibility and Trial Optimization
Gather data, benchmarks, and modeling inputs to support feasibility and trial optimization planning.
Support program review development, including content review and escalation of requirements as needed.
Plan timelines for validation, deliverable development, stakeholder alignment, presentation preparation, and country validation requests.
Support validation and Clinical Trials Allocation Committee activities, including scenario planning, risk table inputs, validation review, modeling updates, and final allocation requests.
Author the initial Global Trials Optimization Report and maintain subsequent report updates throughout the trial lifecycle.
Complete recruitment needs assessments and ensure trial-level GTO reports remain current and actionable.
Recruitment and Retention Planning
Lead early recruitment and retention planning during feasibility, including inputs for project cost estimates.
Develop initial recruitment needs assessments and, where applicable, program-level recruitment budget estimates.
Submit vendor requests and prepare recruitment and retention plans.
Partner with legal on concept reviews, vendor proposal reviews, scope of work finalization, and material or tactic reviews.
Ensure recruitment and retention plans, including enrollment support materials, are implemented effectively.
Oversee enrollment support material development and tactic execution.
Provide required materials to the Metrics, Analytics & Performance team to support accurate Study Optimizer plan entry.
Request and manage appropriate system updates as trial needs evolve.
In-Life Trial Management
Partner with study teams to identify enrollment challenges, assess risks, and recommend potential mitigations.
Manage routine enrollment support materials and vendor activities.
Monitor enrollment performance and prepare standard reporting.
Analyze performance trends and identify opportunities for enhanced support.
Coordinate enhanced enrollment support activities, which may include:
Rescue site and country activities
Internal recruitment and retention refresher meetings
External recruitment and retention booster meetings
Additional participant- or site-facing materials
Rescue vendor engagement
Advocacy engagement and community outreach

Experience supporting clinical trials, feasibility, recruitment planning, enrollment strategy, or trial optimization.
Strong ability to gather, interpret, and apply data to support planning and decision-making.
Experience coordinating timelines, deliverables, stakeholder reviews, and cross-functional inputs.
Ability to work with clinical trial teams, vendors, legal, analytics, and other business partners.
Strong written communication skills, including the ability to develop clear reports, plans, updates, and study-facing materials.
Detail-oriented approach with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced clinical research environment.

Oncology clinical trial experience, especially in lung or breast cancer studies .
Prior experience as an oncology site coordinator .
Experience with recruitment and retention vendors, enrollment support materials, or patient/site-facing recruitment tactics.
Familiarity with enrollment monitoring, performance analysis, country validation, risk tables, or trial allocation processes.
Why This Role Matters
Successful clinical trials depend on reaching the right participants, supporting sites effectively, and responding quickly when enrollment challenges arise. As a Global Trials Optimization Specialist, your work will directly support smarter planning, stronger recruitment strategies, and more effective trial execution.
You’ll have the opportunity to influence global study planning, collaborate with experienced clinical research partners, and help improve how trials connect with patients and sites.
Candidate Profile
We’re especially interested in candidates with oncology trial experience and a strong understanding of site operations, enrollment strategy, and recruitment/retention planning. Internal candidates will be prioritized initially; external candidates may be considered after the initial internal review period.
If you’re a clinical research professional who enjoys bringing structure, insight, and strategy to trial enrollment planning, we’d like to hear from you. Apply today to help support meaningful clinical trials through thoughtful feasibility, recruitment, and optimization work.

Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We believe that there is a better healthcare world – one powered by data. Our platform transforms complex, diverse data into a unified foundation for health, helping organizations deliver better care, boost revenue, and lower costs.
We’re a team of fiercely driven individuals committed to making healthcare more sustainable—and we’re looking for passionate people to help us get there.
For more information, visit .
Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia
At Arcadia , the Enterprise Implementation Manager (EIM) is the customer's primary point of accountability from contract signature through the life of the relationship.

The EIM manages a portfolio of enterprise accounts, leading each customer through onboarding and the technical work required to bring them live — including project managing new data connector builds — but the role exists to protect and grow the value the customer realizes from Arcadia 's platform.

EIMs proactively build the client relationship, drive adoption, resolve risk before it threatens retention, and act as the customer's trusted advisor long after go-live, ensuring customer value is clearly tracked & regularly reviewed.
The ideal candidate is a relationship-first operator: someone who can run a technical delivery workstream competently, but who is just as comfortable owning a client conversation, coaching a teammate, or spotting an account risk before it becomes a retention problem.
What Success Looks Like
In 3 months
Complete onboarding and current product and enablement certifications; build a working understanding of the platform, data model, and Arcadia 's customer success playbooks. The optional Arcadia Certified Professional program is available for continued growth. Shadow tactical client touchpoints and status conversations to learn how EIMs build trust and manage expectations across a client relationship
Take ownership of a defined workstream — for example, project managing a new data connector build — with support from your manager and technical partners
In 6 months
Independently manage cross-team workflows (data integration, configuration, connector builds) while keeping priorities visible and surfacing risk early
Lead tactical client conversations and standing touchpoints, delivering clear, timely updates that keep stakeholders aligned and confident
Proactively identify and escalate delivery or account risk, applying established playbooks to resolve issues efficiently and maintain momentum
Begin building trusted relationships with client stakeholders, understanding their unique technical and business priorities
Contribute to Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), Executive Business Reviews (EBRs), or steering committees for your accounts, and become fluent in maintaining account health scores in Planhat
Build fluency with Arcadia 's customer feedback channels, including the Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT), as part of engaging your accounts
In 12 months
Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts as the primary point of contact — coordinating delivery, connector project management, and ongoing value acceleration & account health under one roof
Drive accountability for on-time, high-quality delivery of commitments, from new data connector implementations to platform adoption milestones
Independently lead recurring QBRs, EBRs, or steering committees, and own the Planhat health score and NPS trajectory for your portfolio, working toward a consistently green status
Partner effectively with the Customer Growth and Retention (CGR) team on renewal and expansion conversations, providing account context and continuity while CGR owns the commercial process
Identify and document process or value improvements, contributing refinements that strengthen delivery consistency and customer outcomes
Share lessons learned and best practices with peers, informally mentoring newer EIMs and Project Associates
What You'll Be Doing
Customer Relationship & Trust
Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts, serving as the customer's primary point of contact throughout the engagement.
Lead tactical status conversations and standing project meetings, delivering clear, timely updates on progress, risk, and next steps.
Facilitate regular touchpoints to align priorities, answer client questions, and maintain stakeholder trust.
Prepare accurate, client-ready documentation and materials that support transparent communication.
Account Health & Governance
Serve as the customer's primary point of accountability for delivery outcomes and overall account health across your portfolio.
Lead recurring QBRs, EBRs, or steering committees with client leadership, tying progress to shared goals, ROI, and next steps.
Maintain each account's health score in Planhat, incorporating usage, engagement, and other signals; own the goal of moving accounts toward a consistently green status. Contribute to your segment's (Core, Enterprise, or National) Net Promoter Score (NPS), which factors into incentive compensation at the segment level rather than by individual account.
Build fluency with Arcadia 's customer feedback channels — including CSAT — as part of the company's growing Voice-of-Customer program.
Partner with the CGR team on renewal and expansion conversations, providing account context, continuity, and delivery insight; CGR owns the commercial renewal and upsell process.
Proactively identify and escalate delivery and account risk; apply established playbooks to resolve issues efficiently.
Maintain project and account momentum through consistent follow-through and clear ownership of open items.
Drive accountability for commitments by managing dependencies and communicating progress across all workstreams.
Implementation & Data Connector Project Management
Project-manage new data connector builds and platform configuration workstreams from kickoff through validation and go-live.
Ensure smooth data orchestration through configuration validation, and maintain detailed documentation of process flows and integrations.
Partner cross-functionally with Data & Health Platform (DHP) teams and engineering to resolve data alignment issues and strengthen reporting reliability.
Cross-Functional Coordination
Manage workflows to maintain alignment and efficiency across internal teams, third parties, and the client.
Coordinate delivery activities and track interdependencies so priorities stay visible and risks surface early.
Ensure project team collaboration and escalate promptly if a workstream is tracking behind.
Value Realization & Continuous Improvement
Identify and document process or workflow enhancements that improve customer outcomes and internal efficiency.
Contribute to continuous improvement by sharing refinements and strengthening knowledge capture across projects.
Connect delivery and account activities to the customer's broader adoption and value-realization goals.
Coaching & Knowledge Sharing
Share lessons learned and best practices from client engagements with peers and newer team members.
Apply feedback to continuously refine your own skills and performance, modeling a growth mindset for the team.

A major function of the Office of Data Acquisitions is to provide databases developed from state highway safety related data for use in analyses aimed at reducing deaths, injuries, crashes, and medical costs.

As the Director, the incumbent will be responsible for the following: Advising the Associate Administrator on all matters related to the design, development, coordination, and management of crash investigation and data collection, and their contribution to achieving the mission of NHTSA.

Keeps the Associate Administrator fully informed as to the status of programs and of problems and controversial issues.

Collaborates closely with the Associate Administrator and other top officials of NHTSA to identify the agency's crash research and data needs, to determine techniques and methods by which the office can meet those needs, to estimate the cost and time required to meet the needs, and to determine other implications of changes.

Carrying out personnel management responsibilities for a staff of professional, technical, administrative and clerical support personnel. Makes decisions on work problems presented by subordinate supervisors and key specialists.

Evaluates performance of subordinate supervisors and reviews evaluations made by supervisors of subordinate employee's performance. Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the State Data Reporting Systems Division responsible for the crash record-based data.

Crash record based data includes the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), a fundamental national data base on traffic safety, Crash Report Sampling System (CRSS), Not-in-Traffic System (NTS) and the State Electronic Data Collection Program (SEDC)., The Division also provides the expertise in sample design and quality control to the other offices in the National Center for Statistics and Analysis, the rest of NHTSA and other offices in DOT.

Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the Crash Investigation Division (CID), provides executive leadership in the planning, design, development, coordination, and management of national networks of motor vehicle traffic crash research and data collection activities.

These include the operation of a national system to conduct detailed investigations of a well-defined selection of motor vehicle crashes currently the Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS)); and the Special Crash Investigations (SCI) program of special investigations of crashes of particular, interest; and Systems for collecting, supplementing, and coding data from police crash reports to provide special purpose data files.

Maintaining liaison with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, police agencies, hospitals, private safety groups, motor vehicle and equipment manufacturers, crash research and analysis organizations, professional societies, and other groups with an interest in crash investigation and crash data for the purposes are for exchanging crash data and information on crash research technology, encouraging the use of crash data, and cooperating on crash research programs.

The ideal candidate is a data executive and systems expert with a track record of managing federal data collection, automation, and national crash investigation programs.

They possess the strategic and technical skills to lead multi-disciplinary teams while directing the human resource, budgetary, and procurement parameters vital to national highway safety initiatives.

A skilled collaborator, they excel at building partnerships across federal, state, and private sectors including law enforcement, public health, and the automotive industry to secure cooperation and advance data systems.

Furthermore, they bring expertise in data governance, enforcing quality control and data completeness while protecting individual privacy, ensuring the delivery of accurate databases that support national safety research and rulemaking.
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience qualifications.

To qualify for the Grade 15, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equal or equivalent to the GS-14, it must include: Experience directing multi-disciplinary professional, technical, and administrative teams while managing the organizational, human resource, and budgetary parameters vital to national highway traffic safety initiatives.

Experience communicating with system managers, rulemaking engineers, researchers, technicians, traffic safety administrators, Governor's Representatives for Highway Safety, State and local officials, national data system program managers and others associated with the application of data as it applies to helping solve complex safety issues.

Experience establishing policy and overseeing large federal data divisions to ensure data completeness, security, and rigorous quality control. Examples include working with executive leadership to plan, develop, and manage large-scale national data collection systems and multi-level crash investigation programs.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Technical Knowledge: Knowledge of federal budgeting to manage large divisional funds, appropriations, large-scale national data architecture, data collection methodologies, complex procurement or contracting mechanisms and systems engineering principles required to build and sustain nationwide databases.

Leadership and Supervision: Management and/or team leader skills, including the ability to direct, manage, and develop a diverse, high-performing human resources workforce of technical and administrative staff.

Communication: Communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, including the ability to secure community support, build strategic intergovernmental alliances, and establish private-sector data-sharing partnerships.

Reasoning: Ability to collaborate across federal, state, and private boundaries to improve data accessibility while balancing competing stakeholder priorities.

For all types of consideration, experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Sie setzen sich ein für die Wahrnehmung der Schule als gestalterisches Kompetenzzentrum. Sie unterstützen die Umsetzung des technischen, digitalen, wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Wandels.
* Die Förderung branchenspezifischer Interessen und die Pflege des Netzwerks mit Verbundpartnern sind Ihnen wichtig.
* Im Schulleitungsteam sind Sie verantwortlich für die Entwicklung mehrerer Bereiche, z. B. ein oder mehrere Berufsfelder der Grundbildung, Weiterbildung, Kurswesen, Veranstaltungen oder Qualitätsmanagement - je nach Ihren Stärken und der aktuellen Neuausrichtung der Schulleitung.

* Studienabschluss Tertiär A oder B in einem an unserer Schule unterrichteten Beruf bzw. einer entsprechenden Studienrichtung und Diplom als hauptberufliche Berufsschullehrperson oder Lehrdiplom für Höhere Fachschulen im Hauptamt

Ashley Digital is the e-commerce engine behind Ashley Furniture Industries — one of the most recognized home brands in the world. As the world's largest manufacturer of home furnishings and the largest furniture store brand in North America, Ashley is in a category unto itself.

We're a fast-moving, highly collaborative team operating at a transformational moment, and we're charged with shaping how people discover, explore, and buy home furnishings. Our expertise spans data science, performance marketing, product, and creative, and our work reaches millions of customers every day.

It's a rare combination: the energy of a tech company, the stability of an industry leader, and the opportunity to build something truly significant. If you're energized by transformation, collaboration, and meaningful impact at scale, Ashley Digital is where ambition meets opportunity.

This individual will partner closely with senior leadership to own the structure and quality of the company's financial and operational reporting cadence — including MBRs, QBRs, and business infrastructure read-outs — ensuring information is accurate, well-organized, and decision-ready. At its core, this role is about synthesis and precision.

You will take financial, operational, and cross-functional inputs and translate them into sharp, structured outputs that reflect what matters most. This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable operating in ambiguity and executing at a high level of detail.

Success requires strong judgment, exceptional work ethic, and the ability to consistently produce high-quality work under tight timelines.

Join the FIA and lead a pioneering safety technology programme.
As F1 Augmented Reality Project Manager within the FIA Technical Department, you will lead a strategic multi-year programme exploring how Augmented Reality and Head-Up Display technologies could enhance driver safety and situational awareness, particularly in conditions of reduced visibility.
You will act as the programme’s technical leader and systems integrator, coordinating specialised suppliers, research partners, Formula 1 teams and internal FIA stakeholders.
This is not a traditional project management role. It requires the technical knowledge to challenge engineering proposals, manage integration risks and drive complex technical decisions.
This new permanent, full-time position is based in Geneva.

Technical programme leadership
Define and own the multi-year technical roadmap, development phases, milestones and deliverables.
Structure the programme across key technologies, including helmet and visor displays, optical HUD solutions, sensors, vehicle positioning, data processing and sensor fusion.
Lead the programme from technology assessment and proof of concept through prototype development, integration and testing.
Maintain effective governance through risk, dependency, resource and milestone management.
Systems integration and technical coordination
Act as the technical systems integrator across on-car electronics, sensors, communication systems, data-processing solutions and driver equipment.
Translate safety and operational objectives into technical requirements, system architectures and validation plans.
Identify technical dependencies, interface constraints and integration risks across hardware and software systems.
Ensure that solutions address Formula 1 constraints, including packaging, weight, aerodynamics, cooling, latency, reliability and driver safety.
Supplier and stakeholder management
Identify and coordinate specialised technology suppliers, engineering partners and research organisations.
Review and challenge supplier proposals, technical architectures, test results, costs and delivery timelines.
Build alignment across Formula 1 teams, FIA technical departments, safety specialists and external partners.
Lead technical workshops, reconcile competing requirements and facilitate pragmatic compromises.
Testing, human factors and risk management
Coordinate simulation, laboratory evaluation, prototype development and vehicle-based testing.
Develop validation protocols for individual technologies and integrated solutions.
Assess human factors, including cognitive workload, visual ergonomics, information prioritisation, latency and emergency driver egress.
Identify and mitigate technical, safety, financial, intellectual property and programme-delivery risks.
Regulatory and strategic roadmap
Assess potential implications for FIA Technical, Sporting and Financial Regulations.
Support the development of regulatory, standardisation and implementation roadmaps.
Prepare technical trade-off analyses, recommendations and phased implementation scenarios.
Consolidate technical findings and test results into clear reports for senior leadership and governance bodies.

Master’s degree in Systems Engineering, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Control Engineering, Embedded Systems, Avionics, Optronics or a related discipline.
Minimum 7 to 10 years of relevant engineering and project management experience involving complex electronic, control or safety-critical systems.
Strong technical knowledge across areas such as vehicle electronics, control systems, sensors, communication systems, sensor fusion, positioning technologies, embedded systems or optical displays.
Experience in Formula 1, WEC or advanced motorsport. Relevant experience from aerospace, avionics or advanced automotive engineering is also welcomed.
Proven experience coordinating complex engineering programmes involving multiple suppliers and interconnected technical workstreams.
Experience integrating hardware and software components within demanding, high-performance or safety-critical environments.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to reconcile competing technical priorities.
Experience with HUD technologies, helmet systems, sensor fusion, vehicle positioning or driver-assistance technologies would be an advantage.
Full professional proficiency in English.
